title: How Moten's and Page's rhythm sections joined to make Basie's rhythm section
summary: Moten played one and three, Page two and four; together they made four, which Jones says is the root of Basie's rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Bass too, but I mean this is a thing, this is a wedding now. Then Walter Page gave up his band and he joined the band along with Dan Minor and Buster Smith and what have you. And you must remember, I can explain to you why the rhythm section of Basie's band the first time - he always had a sax section and a brass section. Bennie Moten played one and three. Walter Page played on two and four; but when they wedded together you had one, two, three, four. The two mediums met, from the one and three, one and three, as against the two and four... Yes, without exaggerating...and they got in that and when that rhythm section - it all come from the rhythm section.
